section_title: What does the king acknowledge after the rescue?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 28 Nebuchadnezzar declared, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him. They violated the king’s command and risked their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God. 29 Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. For there is no other god who can deliver in this way.” 30 Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

context_lines: Nebuchadnezzar blesses the God who sent His angel and delivered the servants who trusted Him. He recognizes that they risked their lives and disobeyed his command rather than worship another god.

He then issues a decree against speaking offensively about their God and promotes the three within Babylon’s province. The ruler who demanded their death now publicly acknowledges the One who saved them.
His new threat of violent punishment remains the king’s decree. The account records it as part of his response, rather than giving God’s people a command to use the same methods.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/daniel/3.htm) sees the rescue as encouragement for Jews in captivity to remain faithful. He also distinguishes the king’s strong conviction in this moment from a lasting change in his conduct.
The story ends with God’s servants preserved and His power acknowledged. The king’s later life is still to be told.
